page: Google Cloud Platform m1-megamem-96 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for workloads requiring extensive RAM capacity. The underlying system utilizes dedicated Intel Xeon processors configured with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs via two threads per core. The processor subsystem incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 38 MB L3 cache, supporting standard vector and bit-manipulation extensions including AVX and AVX-512F. System memory totals 1,434 GB, providing an expansive allocation ratio of approximately 14.93 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate distinct performance characteristics across compute and memory subsystems. Stress-ng multi-core testing yields top-tier throughput, supported by strong uncached memory read bandwidth measuring 201.93 GB/sec and cached read speeds reaching 3,918.5 GB/sec. Large-block write bandwidth sits at an average 89.97 GB/sec. In contrast, single-core CPU metrics, including Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression tests, reflect weaker per-core processing rates. The instance does not include bundled local storage, nor does it feature GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating networked block storage for persistent data.

From a resource utilization standpoint, the instance emphasizes density in volatile memory over raw single-threaded compute speed. This architecture provides operational cost efficiency for deployments constrained primarily by working memory capacity rather than processor clock frequency, avoiding the need to over-provision computing cores solely to access terabyte-scale RAM. Google Cloud Platform m1-megamem-96 is primarily fitted for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise key-value stores, distributed caching tiers, and memory-intensive enterprise analytics.
description: Google Cloud Platform m1-megamem-96 is a memory-optimized instance built around 96 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs across 48 physical cores and 1,434 GB of system memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading, the instance provides roughly 14.93 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware benchmarks reveal strong multi-core throughput and high uncached read memory bandwidth exceeding 201 GB/sec, alongside average write performance. Conversely, single-threaded CPU tasks and sequential compression reflect lower per-core efficiency. The instance features no local storage or attached GPUs, requiring external persistent disks for durable storage operations. Network allocation includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Given its high RAM density and moderate compute performance, m1-megamem-96 presents an efficient infrastructure profile specifically for scenarios where large working datasets must reside entirely in volatile memory. It is best suited for massive in-memory databases, large Redis or Memcached clusters, SAP HANA installations, and high-footprint enterprise batch processing.
